top_stories.title: Nurturing agentic AI beyond the toddler stage
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review explores the development of agentic AI systems—AI that can act independently to accomplish goals—and strategies to ensure such agents are safely aligned with human values as they become increasingly autonomous. The article discusses new technical approaches and presents challenges for business and governance as more capable agentic systems enter industries.

top_stories.title: The Download: glass chips and “AI-free” logos
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review's news roundup highlights the push for glass photonic chips to accelerate AI applications by consuming less power, as well as the emerging trend of 'AI-free' branding. Companies are now labeling products to appeal to consumers wary of AI, indicating how AI's presence is affecting business strategies and public perception.

top_stories.title: Securing digital assets against future threats
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review examines strategies for protecting digital assets—including sensitive business and intellectual property—against future threats posed by advances in AI, such as sophisticated cyberattacks and data manipulation. The article discusses evolving best practices and their implications for organizations and legal frameworks.

top_stories.title: ImportAI 449: LLMs training other LLMs; 72B distributed training run; computer vision is harder than generative text
top_stories.summary: ImportAI's latest newsletter details the trend of using large language models (LLMs) to train other LLMs, a milestone distributed training run at 72 billion parameters, and why computer vision remains more complicated for generative AI than text. This issue provides insight into current technical breakthroughs and their implications for AI businesses.

top_stories.title: Market research is a $100 billion industry. AI will make it a trillion-dollar one.
top_stories.summary: A report covered by Google News investigates how AI is set to transform the market research sector from a $100 billion industry to a potential trillion-dollar market. The article examines AI-driven efficiencies, new business models, and changes in how companies collect and interpret customer data for competitive insights.
